items.evidence: The file opens with '## The bottom line' and then, in order, '**1. What FRUS answers directly.**' (the four changes of rule, 1868 to 1963), '**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**' (Central Decimal File subfiles, the despatch and instruction series, six lot files) and '**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**' (the Estrada declaration, the 1947 study, decisions after 1980). 'Scope' and '## Decisions this needs from you' follow, and '## Findings' begins only after them.

No '%' or 'percent' occurs anywhere. Every figure names what it counts: 'about 940 documents in 87 volumes' and 'from 87 of the 553 volumes'; 'nearly nine in ten of those with a stated source'; 'Across all 553 volumes the doctrine is named in 28 documents'; 'Only one document in the scope is dated in the 1980s, against about 6,000 dated documents from that decade'; 'eight documents that place "recognize" near "states" and "governments"'; 'I read 39 documents in full'; 'the 26 documents cited here'. The weakest two still carry a base: 'only about one document in fourteen carries such a citation' names its set only by the paragraph it sits in (the scope's printed documents), and 'the wider net is about four-fifths on topic by a hand check (see the memo)' gives no sample size.

All 26 documents are cited as the printed edition with a link, e.g. '(Papers Relating to Foreign Affairs, 1868, Part II, Document 632, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1868p2/d632)', '(Foreign Relations of the United States, Diplomatic Papers, 1936, The American Republics, Volume V, Document 112, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1936v05/d112)', '(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume XXI, Chile, 1969–1973, Document 361, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76v21/d361)'. The only short forms are continuations inside a parenthesis that has just given the volume in full, each with its own link: 'see also Document 244, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1895p1/d244', 'same volume, Document 119, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1948v09/d119', 'see also Documents 438 and 1088, https://…/frus1944v07/d438, https://…/frus1944v07/d1088'. Nothing is cited by a bare id pair or by title alone: with every link stripped, no 'frus…' string remains. The 34 links resolve to 26 distinct documents, and the collection file holds exactly those 26.

Part 3 states its absences as searches: '(a) … A search for "Estrada" with any form of "recognize" in documents dated January 1929 to June 1931 found two documents, and neither is the declaration. Across all 553 volumes the doctrine is named in 28 documents, the earliest from 1931, always second-hand.' '(c) Decisions after 1980. Only one document in the scope is dated in the 1980s, against about 6,000 dated documents from that decade. … A lead for the late 1970s (eight documents that place "recognize" near "states" and "governments") was found but not read. All searches ran with a control phrase found in every volume searched and an impossible string found in none.' The scope's own terms are given under 'Scope' ('"recognize" stands within six words of junta, regime, de facto, provisional, military or new government'). Two softer points: the control phrase is never named (other overviews name 'Department of State' and its 552 of 553), and item (b), the 1947 study, rests on the editors' own note ('the editors note that it was not printed and give no file number') rather than on a search.

With every history.state.gov link removed, a scan finds no 'frus…/d…' id string and no bare 'dNNN'. There is no SQL keyword, no snake_case or table/column name ('volume_id', 'document_id', 'body_text' and the like are absent) and no file path; the memo is referred to only as '(see the memo)' at lines 11 and 15, never by a filename or path. Archival identifiers such as '816.01', 'entry A1 3159' and 'identifier 1750062' are finding-aid references, not index names.

judge:r11.rankingReason: r7: the fullest answer (58 documents, 84 retrieved, six findings 1865–1980), every share given over a named denominator, eight lot files with identifiers and access, and four absences each stated as a search with its control count; dense, but nothing a historian would have to redo. r2: 41 documents with full citations throughout, the clearest part 2 and 3 (bulleted, every count with its base, a control pair per search), and the honest candidate-versus-count distinction (23 of 40 sample). r5: 56 documents, quotations set off with full citations, terms explained for a lay reader, measured absences and two unsearched stretches named; its part 3 opens with one assertion. r1: 45 documents in block quotes with citation lines, a four-part cannot-get with counts, six decisions; part 2 is a wall of text and one 'FRUS 1948 … Document 7' lacks a link. r6: 43 documents over 1877–1973 including the Legal Adviser's rule and the 1950s, very detailed shelves, but its bullet quotations cite '(1877, Document 222)' with neither edition nor link. r9: 34 quoted of 59 read, the sharpest late quotations (Haiti 1950 and 1957, Kissinger 1970, Nicaragua 1979), measured absences; citations shortened to '(1913, Document 1047, link)' and no 1980s item. r11: passes all five items cleanly with a coherent six-period answer from Seward 1867 to Chile 1973 and full citations, but rests on only 26 documents, skips the 1950s (admitted under 'Threads not followed'), gives moderate shelves and never names its control phrase. r8: 52 read with vivid quotations (Lind's four conditions, the Haiti 1950 and El Salvador 1960 notes), but no finding before 1913 though its scope starts in 1895, no links on any bottom-line citation, and a part 3 whose first item is a limit of the run's reading rather than of FRUS. r3: 38 documents, but most citations omit the document number (one gives volume and link only), the Hughes 1923 briefing was read in part, and its first 'cannot get' is a finding, not an absence. r4: well-formed and measured, with named controls, but only 19 documents and five findings, the thinnest evidence base of the ten.

items.evidence: queries.log line 1 is the coverage query and memo M1 reports it: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id), COUNT(*), SUM(is_front_matter), SUM(is_editorial_note) FROM document_cache;` -> `553|321749|1103|8481`. Re-run by the scorer: identical.

Memo M1: "The index holds all 553 volumes of the series ... every count below is conditional on these 553 volumes." Overview: "I worked from the full FRUS Explorer index of all 553 volumes"; "About 940 documents from 87 of the 553 volumes".

Memo cites every document as a pair, e.g. M5 "frus1929v03/d657 (Feb 1929, Morrow on Mexico–Nicaragua) and frus1932v05/d775", M7 "frus1868p2/d632"; collection entries carry volumeId/documentId; the overview gives the printed citation plus the canonical URL that carries the pair ("Document 632, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1868p2/d632"). Nothing is cited by title alone.

`rowid` occurs 0 times in queries.log (2,513 lines), memo.md, overview.md, every .py and the collection file; all keys are (volume_id, document_id), e.g. readdocs.py `WHERE volume_id=? AND document_id=?`; the only integer-keyed table (cross_references.id) was never queried.

Every JOIN in the log is on the pair: `JOIN document_cache c ON c.volume_id=f.volume_id AND c.document_id=f.document_id` (log lines 24, 37, 42, 1318), `USING(volume_id,document_id)` (lines 27–36), `LEFT JOIN document_dates d ON d.volume_id=f.volume_id AND d.document_id=f.document_id` (line 1331); Python-side joins key on the pair too (decades.py `dates.get((v,d))`, glosscf.py `dates[(r[0],r[1])]`, arch.py `(r[0],r[1]) in Sset`).

Scope queries carry `AND c.is_front_matter=0 AND c.is_editorial_note=0` (scopeB.py; log line 37); scopeA.py drops apparatus (memo M2.2 "apparatus dropped 1"); scorer check of scope_final.tsv: 940 rows, 0 front matter, 0 editorial notes. The one quotation that is editors' apparatus inside body_text is flagged: M7 Q19 "**EDITORS' FOOTNOTE** summarising Rio Resolution XXVI", overview "that wording is the editors' summary, not the Department's". (The 28 "Estrada doctrine" rows the overview counts were not filtered in the memo's query; scorer verified all 28 are non-apparatus.)

document_cache has summary_text and note_text columns (schema read at log line 3), but neither name appears anywhere in queries.log, the scripts, memo or overview (grep 0); the whole-document read selects only `header, dateline, source_note, body_text, length(body_text)` (readdocs.py; 41 `python3(db.py read)` lines).

The run never used cross_references: its only occurrence is log line 4 `sqlite3 -readonly DB ".schema cross_references"`; no query, count or claim rests on the table and `is_broken` appears nowhere in the log, scripts, memo or overview.

Overview: "The index treats words that share a root ("recognize", "recognition") as one word, so every phrase count was checked against the literal text of every hit." Memo M3 shows the check: `"free elections"` 33 FTS docs -> TOLERANT 33 of 33, STRICT 30 of 33, and "A 1.000 tolerant share tests the stemmer only"; `recogni*` is used as a deliberate prefix and the tokenised spelling `"coup d etat"` was used (log line 29).

Memo M4: "citation_era (a citation FORM, not a date): decimal 803, structured 53, subject_numeric 15, lot_file 13, cfpf 5, named_series 4, published 1" — used only as a categorical; all dating is on document_dates.date_iso (M2.5) and the decimal gloss is gated "only where the DOCUMENT is dated 1910–1949".

Memo M4 is headed "Archival channels (never summed)": "CAME-FROM: 894 of 940 docs have a source row" and "POINTED-AT: 90 rows in 66 of 940 docs" are reported apart; overview: "The two lists are separate channels and are not added together."

The memo inlines the SQL behind its own figures (M1 coverage and controls, M2.5 the decade-denominator SELECT, M2.2 the NEAR query, M5 `MATCH 'Estrada AND recogni*'`) and names the script for every other number, whose SQL db.py appended to the log at execution, e.g. line 1318 `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM frus_documents f JOIN document_cache c ... WHERE frus_documents MATCH 'recogni*' AND c.is_front_matter=0 AND c.is_editorial_note=0` behind M2.4's 16,951 (scorer re-ran: 16,951).

Memo M2.3 "32 of 40 on topic"; M2.4 "592 of 2,337 in the chapters vs 16,951 of 312,169 corpus"; M4 "894 of 940 docs", "90 rows in 66 of 940 docs", "of the 726 glossed, 287 are country Government subfiles"; decade table columns "scope docs | of dated docs | per 1,000"; M3 "95 of 95", "30 of 33".

Where FRUS points for the rest.**" split "*Where the printed documents came from:*" (RG 59 decimal subfiles 816.01, 824.01 ...; series 603720 and 593313; lots A1 3159/1750062, A1 1586E/2839192) and "*What the editors cited without printing:*" (lots A1 3157/2363840, A1 1135/2108779, A1 3147/2068466, A1 5376/631695), and "**3. score:r11.notes: All four named files are present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), plus 19 scripts, their outputs and 41 raw document dumps. Independent verification against the read-only database reproduced every headline figure the memo reports (coverage 553|321749|1103|8481; 312,169; 98,970 / 0 controls; 16,951 / 4,263 / 94,049; 28 Estrada rows, earliest frus1931v02/d228 1931-12-16; 2 Estrada-and-recognition docs; 4,415 post-1980; every decade denominator; external_citations earliest 1910-12-06; the eight late-1970s ids); scope_final.tsv has 940 rows in 87 volumes with 0 apparatus, 0 duplicate and 0 Ed2 rows and spans 1863-09-21 to 1980-10-01; all 24 quotations are exact substrings; every quoted span in the overview maps to a verified quote; lot-to-NAID and series resolutions match the bundled finding aids. Judgement calls the adjudicator may want to review: (1) O1 — the overview carries volume/document ids only inside canonical history.state.gov URLs paired with printed citations; I read that as the public address, not a database id pair. (2) O2 — the only numerals not traceable to a memo line are the narrative count 'the rule changed four times' and archival series year-spans ('1910 to 1963', three file-unit spans), which are not counts; the trace table also has one stale row ('about six documents per thousand' is not in the overview). (3) S3 — the per-form split is reported for the four phrases (STRICT vs TOLERANT) and for recogni* vs 'by force', but not per clause for the six NEAR alternatives. (4) S5 — the two Ed2 volumes whose first editions are also indexed are folded out of the scope and the decade denominators; the corpus-wide false-friend denominators (312,169 etc.) are not Ed2-folded (about 0.2%), unstated. Two small memo slips, neither changing a verdict: M4 writes 'centralFileClass 74' where arch_final.out says 75 (rows sum to 90 only with 75), and M3's corpus-wide quick counts are labelled 'FTS rows' without an apparatus filter (the 28 Estrada rows are in fact all non-apparatus). E3 is not_applicable because the run only read the cross_references schema and never queried the table.

headline.note: Re-derived end to end. I re-ran the session's two TEI scans from the 553 XML files with the refuter folder as cwd: chapters.py gave 2,374 rows and latamdocs.py 59,654 rows, both byte-identical to the session's chap_docs.tsv and latam_docs.tsv. headline.claim: The argument below rests on 26 of them, all read whole

headline.claim: nearly nine in ten of those with a stated source come from the Department of State's Central Decimal File (Record Group 59), 1910 to 1963
headline.memoLine: M4 CAME-FROM: '894 of 940 docs have a source row ... decimal 803 ... record_group: 59 in 837 rows'; M8 trace 'nearly nine in ten came-from rows decimal file -> M4, 803 of 894'
headline.note: My run: 894 document_sources rows join the scope; citation_era decimal 803 (89.8%), structured 53, subject_numeric 15, lot_file 13, cfpf 5, named_series 4, published 1; record_group '59' 837; decimal AND RG 59 = 803. Six of the 803 are 1906–1910 Numerical File citations ('File No. 7357/2', frus1907p2 and frus1910, dated 1907–1909) that the index labels 'decimal', so the Central Decimal File proper is 797 of 894 = 89.1%, still 'nearly nine in ten'; the classed decimal rows run 1911-03-27 (frus1911/d612) to 1963-01-24 (frus1961-63v10-12mSupp/d106), so '1910 to 1963' holds. The sentence that follows does NOT hold: 'and above all from the per-country "Government" subfiles' is contradicted by the memo's own M4 (287 Government vs 341 Political affairs of 726 glossed keys) and by my count (8xx.01 = 287, 8xx.00 = 341); and 'The country "Political affairs" files of Mexico (812.00), Bolivia (824.00) and Costa Rica (818.00) come next' is wrong as an ordering, since 812.00 (90) and 824.00 (66) outrank 824.01 (45) and 835.01 (35), and 818.00 (34) outranks 822.01 (23) and 814.01 (21). The ranking inside the Government subfiles (816.01 108 > 824.01 45 > 835.01 35 > 822.01 23 > 814.01 21) is right. The memo's trace row 'about four in ten glossed keys are Government subfiles' has no counterpart sentence in the overview.

refute:r11.fabricationDetails: None. overview.md holds 32 quote-delimited strings and no block quotes (extract_quotes.py). Eighteen are document quotations (Q1–Q6, Q8–Q14, Q16, Q18, Q19, Q24 of the memo's M7, and the three-word 'an established fact' from Q20); the other 14 are short quoted terms that quote no document ("Government", "Political affairs", "Estrada", "recognize" x5, "states", "governments", "by force" x2, "recognition", and the collection's name) and were listed and excluded. quotecheck.py applied the guide's rule to each of the 18 and to the 24 collection excerpts: lower-case, strip to [a-z0-9], split at …/.../[...] (no passage contains one), require each segment in order in header||dateline||source_note||body_text of the exact cited pair. All 42 FOUND. Three overview quotations are shortened forms of the memo's passages ('satisfied that the new Government...' drops the leading 'being'; 'do not proceed to the recognition...' drops 'they'; 'wished to expel from Bolivia...' and 'controls machinery of Govt...' are inner substrings) and each still sits in its document verbatim. The session's own verifyq.py (case-sensitive, whitespace-collapsed) and the app checker agree: 24 of 24 excerpts inside body_text.
refute:r11.miscitationDetails: None. For every overview quotation the pair of the nearest following URL equals the memo's M7 pair (18 of 18); every printed 'Document N' equals document_cache.document_number of that pair (headers.py: 632, 246, 7, 379, 345, 344, 375, 220, 112, 33, 428, 773, 119, 359, 132, 361 ...), and each printed volume title matches manifest.json's title for the volume_id (e.g. 'Papers Relating to Foreign Affairs, 1868, Part II' -> frus1868p2 'Papers Relating to Foreign Affairs, Accompanying the Annual Message ... Fortieth Congress, Part II'; '1961–1963, Volume XII, American Republics' -> frus1961-63v12). Speaker and date attributions were read against the rows (content.py): d632 is Seward to Sullivan, Colombia, 17 Aug 1867 (Mosquera deposed, Santos Acosta recognized de facto); d598 Seward to Pruyn, 9 Nov 1868, Venezuela's provisional government; d246 Olney to Tillman (Ecuador) 6 Nov 1895; d805 Hay to Loomis 18 Nov 1899 ('this Government would simply ignore the fact of a change of government in Venezuela until the question of its recognition should be raised by formal announcement and request'); d7/1913 is the 12 March circular telegram carrying Wilson's statement of 11 March; d379 Lansing to Hale, Tinoco; d345 signed Hughes, quotes Article II and its bar on leaders and their blood relatives; d618 Stimson, 'clear provisions of the Treaty'; d344 Hughes, property rights and the 1917 Constitution; d375 Stimson's release, which also calls the Cuba treaty and others 'other exceptions based on treaties', as the overview's Decisions section says; d220 Welles backing the Nicaraguan president's proposal; d112 Hull to Keena, quoting an enclosed memorandum 'for your own confidential information'; d33 Guani transmitting the committee's recommendation of 24 Dec 1943; d428 Hull, 'not connected with the question of recognition ... a question for determination by the consulting American Republics'; d773 Byrnes, elections convoked not later than 12 May, action in conformity with the other republics; d7/1948 PPS paper naming the 1947 RE study 'Not printed'; d119 Lovett on Res 35 Bogotá; d454 Acheson, Paraguay; d421 Ball, 'suspended relations, as the United States has'; d359 the Triumvirate; d132 'In keeping with international practice ...' is the Department's text and 'whether the new regime promised ...' the editors' footnote on Resolution XXVI of 1965, exactly as the overview flags; d512 Oliver, 'Recognition Doctrine and the Peruvian Crisis'; d361 WSAG 20 Sept 1973, 'recognition of the new government would be announced on Monday, 24 September 1973', and Porter (State) said 'an established fact'. One contextual liberty, not a misquotation or a wrong pair: frus1899/d805 never names Castro (it names Pulido); the overview's 'Hay simply ignored Castro's seizure' supplies the name from history.

Ball, Brazil, 3/30/64–4/21/66' (in scope); presidential-library-catalog.json lists 'Papers of George Ball', LBJ-P83002, NAID 35300981. (22) Eisenhower Library, Dulles telephone conversations: external_citations row frus1958-60v06/d235 'Eisenhower Library, Dulles Papers, General Telephone Conversations' (in scope); the catalog's DDE-1121 (NAID 574937) lists no telephone series, so the catalog neither confirms nor contradicts the series name. The decimal files named in passing for the pointed-at channel (Bolivia, Haiti, El Salvador, Cuba, Peru) match the date-gated glosses 824.00 x5, 738.00 x5 and 738.02 x4, 816.01 x4, 737.00 x4, 723.00 x4. One negative claim is only mostly right: 'The app's bundled archival data gives no entry number, catalog identifier or access status for the Central Decimal File itself' — series-facts-index.json has no row for it and collection-authority.json's 'Central Decimal File 1910–1929' record carries no NAID, but digitized-ranges-index.json names NAID 302021 (NARA's Central Decimal File series) as a bare seriesNaId, and lot-claimants-index.json lists RG 59 series titled 'Decimal Files' (A1 1509A/B, NAID 2165755, 1953–1960) and 'Central Files' (P 81, NAID 2658540, 1959–1963) as claimants of lots; none of these carries an access status.

refute:r11.notes: All four files present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log 2,513 lines) plus the session's scripts and raw/ dumps; scratch written only to /Users/jbotts/frus-analysis/c3/runs/r11/refuter/ (headline.py/.out, quotecheck.py/.out, archival.py/.out, headers.py/.out, content.py/.out, extract_quotes.py, urls.py, chapters.py, latamdocs.py and their re-run outputs). COMMANDS AND RESULTS. Canary: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id), COUNT(*), SUM(is_front_matter), SUM(is_editorial_note) FROM document_cache -> 553|321749|1103|8481; non-apparatus 312,169; a CREATE TABLE on the main database is refused ('attempt to write a readonly database') while CREATE TEMP TABLE works, which is how the 940 pairs were joined. Scope re-derivation: chapters.py and latamdocs.py re-run from the 553 XML files (3.2 GB) -> 2,374 and 59,654 rows, byte-identical to the session's TSVs; then Path A 2,374 -> 2,338 -> 2,337 non-apparatus -> 592 with MATCH 'recogni*' in 36 volumes (= scopeA.tsv); Path B NEAR query 1,772 non-apparatus hits -> 346 (= scopeB.tsv); Path C phrase searches return frus1913/d7 among 3 hits and frus1949v02/d454 among 6, as the memo describes; union 940 in 87 volumes = scope_final.tsv. Decade table reproduced line for line (1860s 4/11,268 ... 1930s 240/40,073 = 5.99 per 1,000, 1940s 249/75,872 = 3.28, 1980s 1/6,038); so 'thickest between 1910 and 1939' holds by rate (4.67/5.99/5.99 against 3.28 for the 1940s), though by raw count the 1940s' 249 exceeds the 1930s' 240, 127 of them in frus1944v07 as the memo notes. Other quantitative claims in the overview, all reproduced: 'about 6,000 dated documents' in the 1980s = 6,038; one scope document in the 1980s (frus1977-80v24/d115, 1980-10-01); 'Estrada AND recogni*' non-apparatus dated 1929-01-01..1931-06-30 -> exactly frus1929v03/d657 and frus1932v05/d775; '"Estrada doctrine"' -> 28 FTS rows, all non-apparatus, none in an Ed2 volume, earliest frus1931v02/d228 (1931-12-16), and all 28 are US-authored despatches, memoranda or instructions, consistent with 'always second-hand'; NEAR(recogni* states governments, 4) dated >= 1969 -> the memo's 8 documents; 'by force' 35 of 2,337 chapter documents (1.5%) against 4,263 of 312,169 (1.4%), recogni* 25.3% vs 5.4%, as M2.4 says; the 'four-fifths on topic' is the session's hand judgment of 40 Path-B documents (32 of 40), which I did not re-judge. Quotation mapping: each overview quotation was paired with the nearest following URL and cross-checked against the memo's M7 pairs (all agree). FINDINGS AGAINST THE OUTPUT (none is a fabrication, mis-citation or failed headline number): (a) the bottom line's 'above all from the per-country Government subfiles' and 'Political affairs files ... come next' misstate the memo's own M4 counts (Government 287 < Political affairs 341 of 726 glossed keys; 812.00 at 90 and 824.00 at 66 outrank every Government subfile but 816.01); the collection's introductionText repeats 'especially the per-country Government subfiles'; (b) '39 documents read in full' (memo M6, overview) is 41 by the log and raw/; (c) the negative claim that the bundle holds no identifier for the Central Decimal File overlooks NAID 302021 in digitized-ranges-index.json and the 'Decimal Files'/'Central Files' claimant series in lot-claimants-index.json (no access status for any of them, so that part holds); (d) 'Hay simply ignored Castro's seizure' adds Castro's name to a document that names only Pulido; (e) memo nits: M4 says centralFileClass 74 where its own output and my run say 75; the trace table carries rows ('about six documents per thousand', 'about four in ten') for wording the overview does not use; six of the 803 'decimal' came-from rows are 1907–1909 Numerical File citations, leaving 797 of 894 (89.1%) for the Central Decimal File proper, which still rounds to 'nearly nine in ten'. Memo claims I did not independently re-measure: the M3 phrase shares and the precision sample's hand judgment.
